approach: Add `check_root_cause_diagnosis(reading, request, continued)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, registered as one `step!` right after `check_code_survey` in `refusing_check`. It applies when the reading has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, and at least one Behavior criterion, and the job reads as a bug fix. A job reads as a bug fix when (a) the request's non-bullet prose has a repair word (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs) or a 'still' phrase (still shows/showed/shown/lists/listed), or (b) a job the reading continues (retry or follow-up, from `continued_jobs`) was itself a bug-fix request, or was rejected after verification with findings that name a symptom ('still shown', 'passes on the base' and similar). It then requires a located root-cause criterion and a Behavior criterion that names a test and satisfies Athena's existing 'fails without the fix' predicate `asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix`. That predicate is made `pub(crate)` (a one-word change in run/mod.rs) so the gate and the revert demonstration cannot disagree. Add `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` and a seventh reading rule in briefs.rs, unit tests, corpus cases, a CHANGELOG Fixed entry and an architecture paragraph. The earlier steward.rs test is dropped (outside the deliverables); the stored-reading effect is covered by a reading.rs test on `check_reading_text`. The gate reads only the reading, request and earlier-job data it is handed, never the repository.

decisions.choice: Fix at the reading gate with a new `check_*` step in `refusing_check`, not in the decisions page code.
decisions.reason: Jobs 20261103-201526-t4qv and 20261103-231808-3gkq moved a filter because the accepted reading never required a diagnosis or a test that fails on the base. `refusing_check` (reading.rs:3192) is the single entry point, and refusal_corpus.rs requires one refusing case per step.

decisions.choice: Bug-fix signal has two parts. (a) Request prose: trim each line, drop lines where `is_bullet` is true, lowercase, split into words with a local splitter that keeps '_' inside a word (`split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric() && c != '_')`), then match whole words fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, or an adjacent pair 'still' + shows/showed/shown/lists/listed. (b) Continuation: any job in `continued_jobs(request, attempt, referenced)` whose own request has signal (a), or which was rejected after verification (`failed == false`, `verdict == Some("fail")`) with a finding containing a phrase from a second const (still shown, still shows, still listed, still lists, passes on the base, passes without the change, not reproduced). Both lists are consts at the check.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 5. Finding 3: the snapshot has no records, and a grep of the repository for ids 20261103-201526-t4qv, 20261103-231808-3gkq and 20261104-054711-kb90 found nothing, so the real request texts of the motivating jobs are unavailable. The user-visible landed work is outcome-worded (HISTORY.txt:75 '46465f3 Show only open, above-limit proposals on the decisions page'; CHANGELOG.md:457 'still showed'), so a request like that has no repair word. Text alone cannot tell it from a feature. The tense variants of 'still' catch the CHANGELOG-style wording. Signal (b) catches the second try: both motivating introspections describe a retry of a job whose findings say decided proposals were still shown and the test passed on the base. `EarlierAttempt` (briefs.rs:1703) carries `request`, `failed`, `verdict` and `findings`, and `continued_jobs` (reading.rs:2636) already picks the retried job and followed-up jobs. A retry of an ordinary rejected feature job is NOT a trigger, so feature retries are unaffected. Finding 5: the local splitter counts '_' as a word character, so `fix_x` and `prefix` and `fixture` do not match; no replace-with-x trick. The signal remains a limit: a first attempt worded only as an outcome ('Show only open proposals') is accepted, and the doc comment, CHANGELOG and corpus case 12 say so. 'regression', 'fixed', 'wrong', 'broken', 'already' and 'fails' stay out of the list because they are ordinary feature prose (earlier critic rounds). Introspection fix requests ('Fix the root cause of a repeated failure', hestia.rs:434) trigger through 'fix' by design.

rejected.option: Keep only fix and bug and state the limit
rejected.why: Leaves outcome-worded requests, which the motivating jobs probably were, through the gate on a first attempt and on retry.

rejected.option: Trigger on every retry of a rejected code job
rejected.why: Feature retries have no root cause to name; false refusals.

rejected.option: Add wrong, broken, already, fixed, regression as triggers
rejected.why: Feature prose false positives (a fixed token budget, report broken links, add regression tests).

An indirect trick (finding 5); the local splitter states the intent directly.

decisions.choice: Root-cause criterion: contains 'root cause' or 'root-cause', a locator stem (where, enter, originat, why, exclud, because), and a concrete location (a backticked span, `names_crates_path` at reading.rs:3454, or a `path_tokens` token (reading.rs:3035) whose last segment holds a '.'); it must not equal a request bullet after `normalised`. Test criterion: kind Behavior, satisfies `crate::run::asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix(&c.text)`, names a test, and equals no request bullet. 'Names a test' means a backticked identifier that is not a cargo command (the span must not start with 'cargo'), or a crates/ path ending '.rs' or containing 'tests/'. A bare 'cargo test' or `cargo test` no longer counts.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in `mod tests` of reading.rs. A `refuses_a_symptom_only_reading`: start from `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])`, one Behavior criterion that only describes page content ('Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the page shows only undecided proposals'), request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it.'. Call `check_root_cause_diagnosis`, `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance`; assert the first refusing step is `check_root_cause_diagnosis` and the message names the missing root-cause criterion and the missing base-failing test criterion. B `accepts_both_criteria`: add 'The root cause is named: decided proposals enter the page from the unfiltered list built in `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` and the filter does not exclude them' and Behavior 'The named test `decided_proposals_are_not_listed`, built from approved and rejected proposals, fails on the base tree and passes with the change'; Ok from the check and the gate. B2: location as plain text xtask/src/site.rs is accepted. C `refuses_copied_boilerplate`: criteria are the request's stock bullets verbatim; refused by the new check. D: no location refused; 'and/or' alone refused; base-failing criterion with no named test refused, including 'Run `cargo test`: tests fail without the change' (finding 4); dropping only the test criterion gives a message naming only that part. E `accepts_this_jobs_own_reading`. F `agrees_with_the_revert_run_predicate`: for each phrase of run/tests.rs:4700-4731 (positive 'A test fails without the fix', 'Tests fail without the change', 'the new test fails on the base', 'the demo test FAILS without it', 'A regression test that fails before the fix and passes after'; negative 'the build never fails', 'a failing check is reported to the user', 'cargo test passes') build a criterion 'The named test `decided_proposals_are_not_listed`: {phrase}' and assert the gate accepts it exactly when `crate::run::asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix(phrase)`; 'the test fails before the change' is refused. G `bug_fix_signal`: request-prose cases (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, 'still shows', 'still showed', 'still lists') trigger; 'prefix', 'fixture', `fix_it` do not. H `continued_bug_fix`: an outcome-worded request ('Show only open proposals above the limit on the decisions page') is accepted with no attempt, refused with an attempt (rejected, `verdict` Some('fail'), finding 'decided proposals still shown; the new test passes on the base'), accepted with a rejected attempt whose findings and request name no symptom, and accepted when the attempt is `failed == true`.
